# Caddy — custom-context-push-url

custom-context with VAADIN_PUSH_URL=/VAADIN/push. The relocated URL resolves against the context, so the browser asks for /app/VAADIN/push, and the passthrough config carries it with no rule of its own.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/app/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/templates/passthrough.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# App at the backend's own path, proxy at the same path. One site block, one
# reverse_proxy, nothing else.
#
# There is no WebSocket configuration because Caddy has none to give:
# reverse_proxy upgrades on whatever path the client asks. That is why this one
# file serves root-context and custom-context (the backend's context path is
# simply passed through) and both of their *-push-url variants. Compare Apache's
# `upgrade=websocket` and NGINX's `map $http_upgrade` + Upgrade/Connection
# headers, both of which this file does without.
#
# X-Forwarded-For, -Proto and -Host are set by reverse_proxy on its own, and the
# client's Host header is passed through unchanged.
:80 {
	import common
	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
